purpose: Independent real-world observations for Pune used to validate (not calibrate) model demand, throughput, speed and LOS (docs/OVERHAUL.md §24). Nothing is fitted to them.

quality_grades.A: recent (2023 or later) direct measurement, unambiguous location
quality_grades.B: direct measurement but older (pre-2020) or secondary-quoted, location clear
quality_grades.C: old and/or location or extent inferred (mapping uncertain), or aggregate

sources.citation: Comprehensive Mobility Plan for Pune City, Pune Municipal Corporation (2008). Table 4.1 (12 h screen-line counts), Table 4.10 (speed and delay survey, peak hour, 19 corridors), annexure Tables 6 and 8 (mid-block CVC peak hour, screen lines 1 and 2).
sources.method: Manual classified volume counts, 12 h (some 24 h), both directions; speed and delay by test car over the peak period (journey and running speed).

sources.citation: Thakur K.B., Lunkad S.P., Shinde C.R., Ram N.C., Purohit V.I. (2017). Congestion of Traffic at Gunjan Chowk Junction, Pune. IJETT 47(2):91-97 (hourly tables as transcribed in backend/observed/diurnal/build_profile.py).
sources.method: Hourly classified counts 08:00-20:00, both directions of Nagar Road (towards Pune Station / towards Nagar Road).

sources.citation: TraffiCure (Lepton Software) 'Best time to leave - Pune': hour-by-hour average speeds, citywide and per corridor, 'measured from real road data' in partnership with Pune City Traffic Police, powered by Google Maps data; 116 measured corridors, data updated 2026-08-19.
sources.method: Probe (Google Maps) travel speeds averaged by hour of day over the route; corridor geometry not published (only end-point names).

sources.citation: TomTom Traffic Index 2025, Pune (city): average travel time for 10 km 33 min 20 s; morning rush 38 min 13 s; evening rush 41 min 40 s; average speed during rush hour 15.1 km/h; congestion level 71.1%.
sources.method: Floating-car (GPS) data over the whole city road network; congestion = extra travel time over free flow.

sources.citation: Khandekar, Bagwan, Karande & Pilaka (2025), NICMAR / Journal Press India ch. 129 (doi:10.17492/jpi/nicmar/2507129), as transcribed in backend/data/observed_counts/pune_west_2026.json
sources.method: Peak-hour classified turning counts at six west-Pune junctions; AM or PM not stated.

sources.citation: UK DfT TAG unit M3.1 Highway Assignment Modelling (May 2026), Tables 2 and 3: GEH<5 for >85% of individual flows; flows within 100 veh/h (<700), 15% (700-2,700) or 400 veh/h (>2,700) for >85%; modelled journey times within 15% (or 1 minute if higher) of observed for >85% of routes.
sources.method: Acceptance criteria (standard practice), not an observation.
